info.title: FortiManager
info.description: Fortinet FortiManager's JSON-RPC 2.0 API for centralized management of FortiGate devices -- policy and object configuration (pm/config), device management (dvmdb), and provisioning workflows (securityconsole). The entire API is addressed through a single generic RPC endpoint rather than per-resource REST paths. Authentication: static API-administrator token (Bearer). Requires FortiManager >= 7.2.2.
info.x-itential-curated: FortiManager's JSON-RPC API is a single generic endpoint (POST /jsonrpc), not a resource-per-path REST surface, so there is no larger vendor OpenAPI/Swagger spec to trim from. This spec exposes that one endpoint with a generic request/response envelope -- the `method` and `params[].url` fields (see the request body examples below, and the repo README) are how a workflow task selects the actual FortiManager object or operation, the same role `fortigate-rest-call` plays for FortiOS's REST surface from IG5.

post.description: Single entry point for every FortiManager operation -- policy/object CRUD under `/pm/config/adom/{adom}/...`, device inventory under `/dvmdb/...` and `/dvm/cmd/...`, and provisioning tasks (install, workflow) under `/securityconsole/...`. Set `method` to the RPC verb and `params[].url` to the target resource path. See the request body examples for common patterns, and the repo README for a fuller list of `url` values by use case.

getManagedDevices.summary: List devices managed in an ADOM

getFirewallPolicies.summary: Get firewall policies from a policy package

addManagedDevice.summary: Add (promote) a FortiGate into management by this FortiManager

installDeviceConfig.summary: Install the assigned policy package to a managed device

200.description: JSON-RPC response envelope. FortiManager returns HTTP 200 for RPC-level errors too -- check `result[].status.code` (0 is success), not the HTTP status code.

bearerAuth.description: FortiManager API-administrator token, generated on the FortiManager for an API user (System Settings > Admin > Administrators, or `execute api-user generate-key <name>` in the CLI). Requires FortiManager >= 7.2.2 -- older releases only support session-based JSON-RPC auth (a session token embedded in every request body), which can't be expressed as an OpenAPI security scheme.

id.description: Request correlation id, echoed back in the response.

method.description: RPC verb. `get` reads; `add`/`set`/`update`/`delete` are config CRUD; `exec` runs an action (install, device add, reboot, etc.); `clone`/`move` duplicate or reorder objects (e.g. policy rules).

verbose.description: Set to 1 for verbose (name-based, human-readable) response data instead of the default ID-based form.

url.description: Target resource path. Common roots: `/pm/config/adom/{adom}/...` (policy/object config), `/pm/config/adom/{adom}/pkg/{package}/...` (policy packages), `/dvmdb/...` (device/ADOM inventory), `/dvm/cmd/...` (device management actions), `/securityconsole/...` (install and provisioning workflows), `/sys/status` (system info).

data.description: Object payload for `add`/`set`/`update`, or action parameters for `exec`. Shape depends entirely on `url` and `method` -- see the request body examples.

fields.description: Optional field projection for `get` -- limits the response to these attribute names.

option.description: Optional `get` modifiers, e.g. `["get meta"]` or `["get reference"]`.

code.description: 0 on success; non-zero FortiManager error code otherwise.

data.description: Result payload for `get`/`exec` calls. Shape depends entirely on the request's `url` and `method`.
